utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, would you mind taking the diagram again, the one that is on the desk? Could you please indicate on this diagram where you were in relation to your house when you saw the burning houses on that morning, and more specifically so, the house of (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: (redacted). I saw her house burning in the room where my children were sleeping, and the room that the bullet came(redacted). I looked through the window and I saw (redacted) house on fire and her mother's house on fire. When I came to the place where I was shut up, I saw (redacted) house on fire, and I did not see my husband's brother's house on fire. That was not on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Show us on the diagram where the window (inaudible) -- when you saw that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: That's where the window was, belonging to 18 (redacted) house, and this is the window where I was before I left. My children slept here. The window was on this side of the house (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is the window facing(redacted), isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that very moment did you see any soldiers around the houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: No, I didn't. They were hidden behind (redacted), which was located next to his house. I could just hear shots being fired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show on the diagram where the shooting came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: They came from (redacted) in the direction of our house, but they were not firing at us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that shooting directed at? Who were they aiming at do you think?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: Probably they were firing to frighten us, because they had nobody to fire at because we hadn't left the house we were in yet. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you stated that you heard (redacted); is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: When I went out of my house and when I came to the place where I was shut in, (redacted) shouted out to his children to come out of the house because (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show on that diagram where (redacted) was, if you saw him, where he was when he called out his family members for them to come out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: (redacted) was located below his house, here in the middle of his field. This was his shed, and he was in the middle of his field (indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I ask you to give us a rough approximation -- of course, it can't be very accurate, but could you indicate the location where he was and put the letter "C" there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you see soldiers close to your house, and if so, when did you see them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please? I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. When did you see the first soldiers around your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: I saw the soldiers from the place I was shut in when they gathered there, because there was a small opening in the door where we were shut in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question is as follows: Did your husband have a weapon in your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: At that time we didn't, but before that we did and our neighbours took it away from us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which neighbours are you thinking of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: Our (redacted) neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you name them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: Yes, they were below our house(redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to rephrase my question. Could you specify to whom, (redacted) your husband gave -- surrendered the weapons? Could you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: (redacted), because he was there. He was the main commander there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have (redacted) in mind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: Yes, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: I knew him. I did not have occasion to have contact with him, but I knew him because he was near my house. (redacted) He lived across the road, stood across the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And according to you, he was the local HVO commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he the brother of(redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you remember approximately when your husband gave him the weapons he had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FF
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness will be questioned by attorney Luko Susak. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Susak:

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, I would like us to move into closed session, because we shall be mentioning certain names that shouldn't be mentioned, but I will be brief with my questions otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. (Closed session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: You have other witnesses, haven't you? Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, this next witness will be a protected witness as well, face and name, and it will be Witness GG.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: And on our list?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Seven?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Number 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Ten. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam. Could you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Moskowitz:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this time, I will hand to the witness a piece of paper, through the usher, with the name of the witness written on it. Please look at it, Witness, and say "yes" or "no" if that is your name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: While we are taking a look at the name, may I ask you whether the statements you gave us for this witness are only two, one dated the 10th of July, '93, the other one, the 3rd of February, '95?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness GG, you have requested protection, and the Tribunal has granted protection for your face and your name. You can be assured that neither your name, nor your face, will be known outside this courtroom. Should there come a time, during the course of your testimony, where you would need to talk about matters that might, through indirection or some connection, tend to identify you in some way, I will ask to go in closed session, and if the Tribunal grants that request, then your voice will remain in this room and will not be heard outside of this room, so that your identity can remain protected. Do you understand and do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Yes. I have no questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To begin, could you just tell us how old you are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Twenty-eight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to April 16, 1993, where did you live?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: In Ahmici, Zume, more precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, during that time period, and I'm not referring to the actual day of April 16, 1993, but during that time period, could you give us an idea of your family, not by giving any names, but by describing relationships? I'm specifically interested in who was living in your house in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: My father, mother, and sister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this a two-level house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there an upper story and a lower story?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe which floor or which level of the house you and your family lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: We lived upstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you be able to get from the upstairs level to the downstairs level in that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: We would have to go out and then go to the other story.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was an outside staircase in order to go from the upstairs to the downstairs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honour, I'm going to request that the witness identify her house more specifically, so I would request going into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. We will move into closed session. (Closed session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: (Open session)

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us the first thing you remember hearing or seeing on April 16, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: The first thing that happened was that shooting woke me up. I got up. A few minutes later, a tracer bullet got into our living room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when the tracer bullet entered your living room? What did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: It fell on the couch, and it started burning. I went to fetch some water, and I tried to extinguish the fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you hear any noises coming from outside your house at this time, any sounds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you try to do anything to summon help in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: I took the telephone so that I could make a call and ask what was going on, but the telephone was out of order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you and your mother then do? I take it now you are on the upper floor at this time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Yes, at the upper floor. That's where we were. I then told my mother that this part of the house was not safe, that it would burn down for sure, and that we should go to the lower part of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to go to the lower part of the house, you actually had to go outside and use the outside staircase; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. You have to go outside, and that is how you get into the lower part of the house, the lower floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anything when you went outside to go down to the lower part of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: From the lower part facing the main road, I saw three soldiers in uniform. On the upper side of the house, there were two soldiers, also in uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell whether they were carrying any weapons at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they carrying weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you recall happening next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: When they saw us, they got together in a group, and they pushed my mother and myself into the lower part of the house, into this room downstairs, and five of them got in, together with my mother and myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these soldiers say anything to you and your mother as they were pushing you back into the lower part of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: They were cursing our balija mothers. When they got in, they started searching the house, and they asked where my father was. It was chaotic. Every one of them had something to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe, a little bit, the room where you and these soldiers were now in on the lower part of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: It was a room. You could walk into this room from the outside. It wasn't very big. It was a living room, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the lights on in this room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How close were you to some or all of these soldiers while you were in the room with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Very close, because it's a smallish room. There were five of us. My mother was there. I was there. That is seven of us altogether, together with all the things that were in there, so we were very close.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long do you think you spent in that room with these soldiers that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Perhaps five or ten minutes, something like that, but it was very long for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Yes. I recognised Anto Furundzija, because, at one moment, one of the soldiers was trying to make me go and call my neighbours. Then I turned around, and I recognised Anto Furundzija. He was a schoolmate of mine. I asked him whether I could take some shoes, as they were making me go outside. I asked him, "What is it? What is going on," because he knew me well and I knew him too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you when you asked him about your shoes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: No, no, nothing, nothing. We didn't answer that question of mine at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: He was in camouflage uniform. He had a Jokers emblem on his sleeve, and he had one black line painted on both of his cheeks, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any trouble at all recognising him as your former schoolmate, Anto Furundzija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I guess my question is: Did you have any difficulty recognising him or did you recognise him immediately as you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: I recognised him immediately, quite clearly, and I addressed him immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: At this time, I would ask the witness be shown formerly admitted Exhibit P249.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us who this person is in Exhibit P249?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Anto Furundzija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the man you saw in your house on April 16, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Yes, but he was a little slimmer then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can we now show the witness previously admitted Exhibit P45?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the Prosecutor is now asking the witness, on the basis of this photograph, to identify a certain individual. However, there is another case against this individual in this Trial Chamber, and I don't think that it is proper that we should carry out an identification of this individual who is being tried in another case. I don't see the purpose of having the identification made here because, in this particular hearing, this is not an accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Radovic, you are right when you say that there is a trial before this same Trial Chamber against Mr. Anto Furundzija, but we have already ruled on this matter, that we will not take into account any evidence tendered in this trial when we make any finding in the other trial. Whatever is said here about Mr. Furundzija will have no relevance whatsoever in the other trial. Of course, this is the basic principle of a fair trial. It would not be fair to Mr. Furundzija to take into account evidence in this trial which has been tendered here. We have already ruled on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: If the witness could now be shown the next exhibit, Exhibit P45.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this look familiar, Witness GG?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Yes. That is the emblem worn by Anto Furundzija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Anto Furundzija have a weapon with him when you saw him in your house that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Yes, he did. I think he had a rifle. Anyway, it was a long barrel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I believe you were saying that, at one point, a soldier asked you to do something. Do you recall what that soldier asked you to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: He asked me to call my neighbours, the neighbours who lived across from my house. He asked me whether there were any menfolk there, and I said that I didn't know. I asked him not to make me go because I had just got up and there was shooting outside. At that moment, the other soldier said, "Get out." My mother and I started to leave, although my mother didn't want to go. She wanted to stay in the room, but they said, "Get out. Go outside."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you were leaving or, perhaps, prior to your leaving the house, did you see any soldiers with any kind of communication device?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: In going out, I looked down, I wasn't allowed to turn around, but I just glanced downwards, and I saw him take up a walkie-talkie or some device of that kind, and he said, "Everything is going according to plan."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When this soldier said, "Everything is going according to plan," was he speaking into this walkie-talkie or was he talking to one of the soldiers in the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: He was saying it into the walkie-talkie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Anto Furundzija in the room when that was being said into the walkie-talkie?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you and your mother left the house on orders of these soldiers, what do you remember seeing or hearing next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS GG
utterances.text: While we were leaving the house, we were in front of the house, and one of the soldiers climbed up onto the stairs leading to the upper story of the house, and he looked in the direction of the house of (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: At this point, Your Honour, I would request that we go back into closed session for a couple more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. (Closed session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
